The method produces a pre-insulated pipe by first positioning a jacket pipe in a guide channel and fixing it securely in place. The guide channel supports and aligns the jacket pipe during the manufacturing process, ensuring that the subsequent insertion of the insulated inner piping can be carried out accurately and efficiently.

A length of insulated inner piping is then provided for insertion into the jacket pipe. This insulated inner piping includes an inner pipe surrounded by a layer of compressible insulation material. The insulation material is selected so that it can be radially compressed during insertion and subsequently expand or press outward again when the compression is released.

The first end of the insulated inner piping is inserted into the jacket pipe from the front end of the guide channel. Once the insulated inner piping has entered the jacket pipe, an overpressure is applied inside the jacket pipe. This overpressure acts on the compressible insulation material and causes it to compress radially around the inner pipe. By reducing the effective outer diameter of the insulation layer, the overpressure facilitates movement of the insulated inner piping through the jacket pipe and reduces friction during insertion.

While the overpressure is maintained, the insulated inner piping is advanced through the jacket pipe until it reaches the desired position. After the insulated inner piping has been moved into place, the overpressure inside the jacket pipe is removed. As the pressure is released, the compressed insulation material expands radially outward and engages with the inner surface of the jacket pipe. This expansion fixes the insulated inner piping in position within the jacket pipe, thereby forming the completed pre-insulated pipe.

A method for producing a pre-insulated pipe comprises providing an outer jacket pipe and arranging the jacket pipe in a guide channel or similar holding device so that the jacket pipe is supported and maintained in a predetermined position during assembly. An inner pipe, which may be a service pipe intended to carry a heating medium, cooling medium, gas, liquid, or other fluid, is provided with an outer layer of thermally insulating material. The insulating material is compressible in the radial direction, so that its outer diameter can be temporarily reduced when pressure is applied.

To assemble the pre-insulated pipe, the insulated inner pipe is introduced into one end of the jacket pipe and advanced longitudinally through the jacket pipe. Before or during this insertion step, an overpressure is generated inside the jacket pipe, for example by supplying compressed air or another pressurized gas into the annular space between the jacket pipe and the insulated inner pipe. This overpressure acts on the compressible insulation surrounding the inner pipe and compresses it radially inwardly. As a result, the effective outer diameter of the insulated inner pipe is reduced, thereby lowering friction and allowing the inner pipe with its insulation to be pushed or pulled into the jacket pipe more easily.

The guide channel holds the jacket pipe steady and prevents undesired deformation or displacement while the insulated inner pipe is being inserted. The overpressure may be maintained throughout the insertion process, or it may be adjusted as required to achieve sufficient radial compression of the insulation. Once the inner pipe has reached its intended position within the jacket pipe, the supply of pressure is stopped and the overpressure inside the jacket pipe is released.

When the pressure is released, the previously compressed insulation expands radially outwardly toward its original shape. This expansion causes the insulation to bear firmly against the inner surface of the jacket pipe, thereby securing the inner pipe in position within the jacket pipe. The resulting product is a pre-insulated pipe in which the service pipe is surrounded by insulating material and enclosed by an outer jacket pipe. The method enables the insulated inner pipe to be inserted with reduced resistance while ensuring that, after pressure release, the insulation provides a tight and stable fit inside the jacket pipe.

1. **A method of producing an insulated pipe assembly**, the method comprising:  
   providing an inner pipe;  
   positioning insulating material around the inner pipe;  
   providing an outer jacket pipe defining an interior passage;  
   introducing a pressurized fluid into the outer jacket pipe to create an overpressure within the interior passage;  
   using the overpressure to temporarily compress the insulating material around the inner pipe; and  
   inserting the inner pipe with the compressed insulating material through the outer jacket pipe while guiding the inner pipe relative to the outer jacket pipe.

2. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the pressurized fluid comprises air.

3. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the overpressure reduces an outer diameter of the insulating material during insertion of the inner pipe into the outer jacket pipe.

4. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the insulating material expands after reduction or release of the overpressure to at least partially fill an annular space between the inner pipe and the outer jacket pipe.

5. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the inner pipe is guided coaxially relative to the outer jacket pipe during insertion.

6. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the outer jacket pipe is supported by a guide arrangement during insertion of the inner pipe with the insulating material.

7. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the insulating material comprises a compressible thermal insulation layer.

8. **The method of claim 1**, further comprising sealing at least one end region of the outer jacket pipe sufficiently to maintain the overpressure during insertion.

9. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the overpressure is maintained at a level sufficient to reduce friction between the insulating material and an inner wall of the outer jacket pipe during insertion.

10. **The method of claim 1**, wherein the pressurized fluid is supplied through at least one inlet communicating with the interior passage of the outer jacket pipe.

11. **An insulated pipe assembly produced by the method of claim 1**, comprising:  
    an inner pipe;  
    an outer jacket pipe surrounding the inner pipe; and  
    a layer of insulating material disposed between the inner pipe and the outer jacket pipe,  
    wherein the insulating material has been inserted into the outer jacket pipe in a temporarily compressed state caused by overpressure within the outer jacket pipe.

12. **An apparatus for producing an insulated pipe assembly**, comprising:  
    a guide configured to guide an inner pipe carrying insulating material into an outer jacket pipe;  
    a pressure supply configured to introduce pressurized fluid into an interior passage of the outer jacket pipe to create an overpressure therein; and  
    a control arrangement configured to maintain the overpressure during insertion such that the insulating material is temporarily compressed around the inner pipe as the inner pipe is inserted through the outer jacket pipe.
